records.real_world_identity_notes: Group C prototype campaigned by Nissan in 1989, powered by the VRH35 3,496cc twin-turbo DOHC V8. Nissan's heritage record specifies a VGC five-speed transmission, matching the five forward gears exercised in the live drive.

additional_claims.basis: The guided drive recorded that a clutchless upshift was accepted after a throttle lift and a clutchless downshift after the driver's manual throttle blip, with no automatic cut or blip detected.

year.label: MRX customer prototype; AMS2 Duratec P4 configuration

records.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian customer sports prototype built by Metalmoro as the successor to the MCR, later revised with a new chassis. 'Duratec' denotes the Ford engine and 'P4' the Endurance Brasil class, neither of which is the marque. The constructor states the MRX accepts diverse engine and transmission options, so no single real-world gearbox is fixed and entrants have run different sequential units. The AMS2 car is one such configuration, and its six-speed sequential stick is established by the live drive rather than by a fixed factory specification.
records.confidence_basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. The constructor establishes the MRX identity but fixes no transmission, so the real-world gearbox for this exact configuration is not independently confirmed.
records.identity_basis: The constructor's own page establishes the MRX as a Metalmoro customer prototype, and the exact simulator identity was observed live. The specific real-world build behind the AMS2 Duratec P4 is not identified.
records.specification_basis: The live drive exercised six sequential gears through a visible sequential stick. The constructor states transmission options vary by customer, so the sequential six-speed is recorded at medium confidence as the configuration modeled in AMS2, not as a fixed factory specification.

additional_claims.basis: The guided drive accepted a full-throttle clutchless upshift with a detected automatic cut, so no lift is required. No automatic blip was detected on downshifts, and this record follows the curated convention for a sequential stick without automatic blip, where the driver supplies the rev-matching blip.
